title.narrative: 7. (1) The labour force employed in North region, number of employees.

description.narrative: This indicator is part of Indicator The labour force employed in North region, number of employees. Rate of the labour force participation in North region, %. The initially proposed KPI in the project Application The rate of jobs created in the North region will be difficult to measure as well as validate by retrieving the relevant data from the official sources, such as NBS, National Employment Agency (NEA). Even though the NBS is collecting data on new jobs for annual research on the Employee mobility and jobs there is no opensource information available in this sense. At the same time, the NEA survey Labour market forecast for 2021 from the employers perspective states that in the statistical region North from 3083 businesses that participated in the survey, only 24% plan to invest and 70% consider that no major increase in goods and services demand will occur, while many entrepreneurs are confronting shortages in the qualified labour force. It is assumed that this trend will be maintained in the coming years. This suggests that most of the businesses will concentrate on consolidation efforts that will bring more robustness to their undertaking by reducing or eliminating the existing weaknesses either caused by labour force shortages, market volatility, pandemic situation or other challenges .Taking into consideration the above, it would reasonable to replace the current KPI with other performance indicators that are easier to access, i.e. available and fully meet all SMART criteria. Moreover, they are fully in line with the EU nomenclature & classification of the statistical data, common criteria and definitions, which are: The labour force employed in the North region, quantified by the number of employees at the end of the year, and; The rate of the labour force participation in the North region, measured in per cent demonstrates the qualitative changes showing the share of the active age population enrolment in the labour market in the region.Both indicators are available in the annual NBS publications. The latest data is available for 2020 and is proposed as temporary reference values that can be updated when the 2021 data is available: 251,100 employees is the reference value for the labour force employed, and; 43% is the reference value for the rate of labour force participation.NOTE: Both indicators are available in the sexdisaggregated form . The data for 2021 will be published in 2022.

title.narrative: 7. (2) Rate of the labour force participation in North region, %

description.narrative: This indicator is part of Indicator The labour force employed in North region, number of employees. Rate of the labour force participation in North region, %. The initially proposed KPI in the project Application The rate of jobs created in the North region will be difficult to measure as well as validate by retrieving the relevant data from the official sources, such as NBS, National Employment Agency (NEA). Even though the NBS is collecting data on new jobs for annual research on the Employee mobility and jobs there is no opensource information available in this sense. At the same time, the NEA survey Labour market forecast for 2021 from the employers perspective states that in the statistical region North from 3083 businesses that participated in the survey, only 24% plan to invest and 70% consider that no major increase in goods and services demand will occur, while many entrepreneurs are confronting shortages in the qualified labour force. It is assumed that this trend will be maintained in the coming years. This suggests that most of the businesses will concentrate on consolidation efforts that will bring more robustness to their undertaking by reducing or eliminating the existing weaknesses either caused by labour force shortages, market volatility, pandemic situation or other challenges .Taking into consideration the above, it would reasonable to replace the current KPI with other performance indicators that are easier to access, i.e. available and fully meet all SMART criteria. Moreover, they are fully in line with the EU nomenclature & classification of the statistical data, common criteria and definitions, which are: The labour force employed in the North region, quantified by the number of employees at the end of the year, and; The rate of the labour force participation in the North region, measured in per cent demonstrates the qualitative changes showing the share of the active age population enrolment in the labour market in the region.Both indicators are available in the annual NBS publications. The latest data is available for 2020 and is proposed as temporary reference values that can be updated when the 2021 data is available: 251,100 employees is the reference value for the labour force employed, and; 43% is the reference value for the rate of labour force participation.NOTE: Both indicators are available in the sexdisaggregated form . The data for 2021 will be published in 2022.

comment.narrative: The indicator is available in the annual NBS publications. The latest data is available for 2020 and is proposed as temporary reference value that can be updated when the 2021 data is available 43 is the reference value for the rate of labour force participation.
Rate of labour force participation increased by 3. The value to be verified with NBS during the evaluation mission in spring 2022
Rate of labour force participation 35 465 according to the NSB.

title.narrative: 7. (2) Rate of the labour force participation in North region, %

description.narrative: This indicator is part of Indicator The labour force employed in North region, number of employees. Rate of the labour force participation in North region, %. The initially proposed KPI in the project Application The rate of jobs created in the North region will be difficult to measure as well as validate by retrieving the relevant data from the official sources, such as NBS, National Employment Agency (NEA). Even though the NBS is collecting data on new jobs for annual research on the Employee mobility and jobs there is no opensource information available in this sense. At the same time, the NEA survey Labour market forecast for 2021 from the employers perspective states that in the statistical region North from 3083 businesses that participated in the survey, only 24% plan to invest and 70% consider that no major increase in goods and services demand will occur, while many entrepreneurs are confronting shortages in the qualified labour force. It is assumed that this trend will be maintained in the coming years. This suggests that most of the businesses will concentrate on consolidation efforts that will bring more robustness to their undertaking by reducing or eliminating the existing weaknesses either caused by labour force shortages, market volatility, pandemic situation or other challenges .Taking into consideration the above, it would reasonable to replace the current KPI with other performance indicators that are easier to access, i.e. available and fully meet all SMART criteria. Moreover, they are fully in line with the EU nomenclature & classification of the statistical data, common criteria and definitions, which are: The labour force employed in the North region, quantified by the number of employees at the end of the year, and; The rate of the labour force participation in the North region, measured in per cent demonstrates the qualitative changes showing the share of the active age population enrolment in the labour market in the region.Both indicators are available in the annual NBS publications. The latest data is available for 2020 and is proposed as temporary reference values that can be updated when the 2021 data is available: 251,100 employees is the reference value for the labour force employed, and; 43% is the reference value for the rate of labour force participation.NOTE: Both indicators are available in the sexdisaggregated form . The data for 2021 will be published in 2022.

comment.narrative: The indicator is available in the annual NBS publications. The latest data is available for 2020 and is proposed as temporary reference value that can be updated when the 2021 data is available 43 is the reference value for the rate of labour force participation.
Rate of labour force participation increased by 3. The value to be verified with NBS during the evaluation mission in spring 2022
Rate of labour force participation 35 465 according to the NSB.
